title: Tuna Noodle Casserole with Vegetables and Cream Sauce

content.title: About
content.content: Tuna noodle casserole with vegetables in a cream (or white) sauce is a baked dish that combines cooked noodles, chunks of tuna, mixed vegetables (such as peas, carrots, broccoli) and a smooth sauce made from cream or milk. The dish is popular in American home cooking as a quick, hearty family meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Canned tuna is commonly used in casseroles because it stores well and has a mild flavor.
The classic recipe appeared in the United States in the mid‑20th century when canned tuna became widely affordable.
The cream sauce is usually made from milk, cream, flour, and cheese, giving the casserole a rich texture.
Variations may replace noodles with rice, quinoa, or gluten‑free pasta for a healthier twist.
Casserole portions are often cut into squares, making them convenient for school lunches and picnics.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Tuna provides high‑quality animal protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Canned tuna contains EPA and DHA, which support heart and brain health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Tuna and dairy ingredients supply B12, B6, and niacin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Vegetables add fiber and micronutrients
items.content: Added vegetables increase dietary fiber, vitamin A, vitamin C, and potassium.

items.title: Calcium from dairy
items.content: Cream and cheese enrich the dish with calcium for bone health.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned tuna often contains added salt; choose low‑sodium versions if you monitor sodium intake.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: Tuna can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: The cream sauce adds saturated fat; a lighter milk‑based sauce can be used as an alternative.

items.title: Mercury in tuna
items.content: While mercury levels in canned tuna are generally low, pregnant women and children should limit consumption.

content.title: How to Prepare and Serve
content.content: Cook the noodles until al dente, combine with tuna, cooked vegetables, and cream sauce. Transfer to a baking dish, top with shredded cheese, and bake 20‑25 minutes at 180 °C (350 °F) until golden. Serve hot, garnished with fresh parsley or chives.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the casserole to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat in the microwave or oven to an internal temperature of 75 °C (165 °F) before serving.
